blocks.text: Ask me where to drink in Bondi and I'll answer before you finish: start beachfront for a sundowner, then wander inland as the night warms up. After years living just back from the sand, these are the ten bars I actually send friends to - ocean-view balconies, heritage pubs, cosy locals' corners and one or two that run late.

items.label: Best for views
items.value: Icebergs, North Bondi RSL, Hotel Ravesis

items.label: Getting here
items.value: Bus to Bondi Beach, or the 333 from the city

blocks.text: My beachfront big-hitters
1. Hotel Ravesis

You can't miss the flamingo-pink corner where Hall Street meets Campbell Parade. [Ravesis](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/hotel-ravesis) is my pick for the whole spectrum in one building - a schooner or a rosé on the terrace early, then upstairs as the DJs get going and it tips into the small hours. Grab a front-terrace spot for the wide view.
2. Icebergs (the Bondi Bar balcony)

For the postcard, nothing beats the balcony bar at [Icebergs](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/icebergs-dining-room-and-bar), above the famous ocean pool at the south end. It's dress-up-a-little and priced for the view, but a negroni at golden hour is a genuinely Sydney moment. It books out - reserve ahead through the Icebergs site, and if you want more tables with that same ocean outlook, see our guide to [beachfront and ocean-view dining](/bondi-eat-and-drink/waterfront-dining-bondi-beach).
3. North Bondi RSL

My tip for the best-value view in Bondi: the [North Bondi RSL](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/north-bondi-rsl) at the north end. Sign in as a guest, head to the wrap-around glass balcony and you get the same knockout beach outlook for far less. Check the RSL's own site for sign-in and hours first.

Bondi faces east, so the sun sets behind you over the rooftops, not the sea. The magic is the glow on the water and the headlands - have a drink in hand about half an hour before sunset and watch the beach turn gold.
Pints, cocktails and cosy corners
4. Hotel Bondi

The grand heritage pub right on Campbell Parade, [Hotel Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/hotel-bondi) has watched over the beachfront for the better part of a century. A quick note for anyone chasing a beer I used to send people out for: Bondi's much-loved microbrewery, Curly Lewis, has sadly closed since I first wrote this list - so a beachfront pub like this is now my easy pick for a cold one near the sand. Grab a spot in the front bar, catch the sport, and you're a minute from the promenade.
5. El Topo

[El Topo](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/el-topo-mexican) is a snug, low-lit spot for agave and cocktails just back from the beach - mezcal, tequila and a margarita list that rewards a bit of adventurousness. It's tight and loud in the best way, and my go-to for kicking a night into gear; there are proper Mexican plates too, so an early stop can easily turn into dinner.
6. Beach Road Hotel

A couple of streets back on Beach Road, [Beach Road Hotel](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/beach-road-hotel) is the reliable all-rounder - cold schooners, pub classics, live sport, and DJs and bands upstairs on weekends. It's where a lot of Bondi nights quietly end up, and one of [Bondi's best pubs](/bondi-eat-and-drink/pubs-bondi-beach) if you fancy a proper crawl.
The rest of my ten
These four round out the list - a different mood for each night.

items: [Beach Bar at Promenade](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/beach-bar-at-promenade-bondi-beach) - beachfront spritzes and people-watching right on Campbell Parade, and a happy stand-in for a feet-in-the-sand summer session now that the Pavilion's Bucket List has closed.
[Neighbourhood](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/neighbourhood-bondi) (Curlewis Street) - a lively little local back from the sand, good for a natural wine with the after-beach crowd.
[The Shop & Wine Bar](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/the-shop-and-wine-bar) (Curlewis Street) - café by day, snug wine bar by night; my pick for a quiet drink and a cheese plate.
[The Stuffed Beaver](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/the-stuffed-beaver) (Bondi Road) - an unpretentious, good-fun bar for burgers, mezcal and a night that doesn't take itself too seriously.

blocks.title: Summer weekends fill fast
blocks.text: From December through February the beachfront venues can hit capacity by mid-afternoon on a hot day. If a table matters - especially at Icebergs or for a big group - book ahead through the venue's own site and confirm current hours.
Grab a bite between rounds

A good crawl runs longer if you line your stomach. Most of these bars do food, but half the fun of Bondi is ducking out between rounds - a taco, a wood-fired slice, a banh mi or a late-night burger are all within a block or two of the sand. Our [cheap eats in Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/cheap-eats-bondi-beach) guide has the best quick bites, or if you'd rather build the night around a proper sit-down, browse our [date-night restaurants](/bondi-eat-and-drink/date-night-bondi-beach).
How I'd string them together

stops.detail: Best-value beach view while the light is still high.

stops.title: Beach Bar at Promenade
stops.detail: Down to the sand for a spritz as the beach turns gold.

stops.detail: Shift gears - a cold pint or a mezcal margarita.

stops.title: Hotel Ravesis or Beach Road
stops.detail: Finish where the DJs are for a late one.

blocks.title: Beyond the bars
blocks.text: Chasing something specific - a rooftop spritz, a natural-wine list, a long lunch with a view? Our full [Bondi eat-and-drink directory](/bondi-eat-and-drink) covers 160+ venues you can filter by cuisine, area, price and who you're with. If you just want the drinking spots, jump to our hand-picked [best bars in Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/best-bars-bondi-beach).

items.q: Which Bondi bar has the best beach view?
items.a: The balcony bar at Icebergs, above the ocean pool, wins for the postcard shot. For the same outlook at a much lower price, head to North Bondi RSL's upstairs balcony. Ravesis' front terrace pairs the view with a livelier crowd.

items.q: Where can I drink late in Bondi?
items.a: Hotel Ravesis and the Beach Road Hotel reliably keep going into the night on weekends, with DJs upstairs. Closing times vary by season, so check each venue's own site for current hours.

items.q: Is there craft beer brewed in Bondi?
items.a: Not any more, sadly - Curly Lewis Brewing Co., Bondi's own microbrewery, has closed, so there's no beer brewed in the postcode right now. For a good tap list your best bets are the beachfront and back-street pubs like Hotel Bondi and the Beach Road Hotel. Our [best pubs in Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/pubs-bondi-beach) guide has the full line-up.

items.q: How do I get to Bondi Beach for a night out?
items.a: The easiest route from the city is the 333 or 380 bus, or the train to Bondi Junction and a beach-bound bus. Check Transport for NSW for timetables and plan your way home before the last service.

items.q: Do I need to book ahead?
items.a: For most pubs and casual bars you can just turn up. For Icebergs, or larger groups on summer weekends, book directly through the venue's site.

blocks.text: That's my ten - enough range for any kind of Bondi night, from a quiet wine after the beach to a full sunset-to-late crawl. Hours and prices move with the seasons, so treat this as the shortlist and confirm details on each venue's own site.

Bondi packs one of Sydney's best café scenes into a few walkable streets behind the beach - beachfront brunch rooms, serious coffee windows, and a run of newer openings worth knowing about in 2026. Below is the shortlist I'd hand a visitor: what each place is known for, roughly where it is, and who it suits. I write these as a local curator rather than claiming to have eaten at every one this week, so treat the details as a well-researched starting point and check current hours before a special trip. For the full, filterable picture - every café and coffee window we've mapped around the beach - there's our [complete Bondi cafés and coffee guide](/bondi-eat-and-drink/best-cafes-bondi-beach).

blocks.title: A living guide
blocks.text: Bondi's café scene moves fast - hours, menus and even owners change. I last reviewed this in August 2026; confirm anything time-sensitive on the venue's own channels before you go.
Best beachfront cafés for brunch
Speedos Café - North Bondi

[Speedos](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/speedos-cafe) sits up at the quieter North Bondi end (Ramsgate Avenue) with some of the best ocean views of any café on the beach. It's the classic post-swim spot - health-leaning brunch, bowls, pancakes and juices, with window benches looking straight out to the water. Best for: a relaxed, view-first breakfast at the north end.
Chapter One - Campbell Parade

Right on Campbell Parade opposite the sand, [Chapter One](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/chapter-one-caf-and-wine-room) is a café-meets-wine-bar that's been going since 2012, pouring Allpress coffee alongside an all-day menu. It's an easy, central choice if you want to be directly across from the beach - one of a handful of genuine [beachfront and ocean-view spots](/bondi-eat-and-drink/waterfront-dining-bondi-beach) around the sand. Best for: an all-rounder in the middle of the action.
bills - Hall Street

The Sydney institution founded by Bill Granger has been on Hall Street (number 79) since 2014, and [bills](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bills-bondi-beach) is still open and busy. Come for the dishes that made it famous - ricotta hotcakes and sweetcorn fritters - in a light, airy room. Best for: a benchmark Bondi brunch and a bit of Sydney food history.
Best for specialty coffee
Harry's Bondi - Wairoa Avenue

[Harry's](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/harrys-bondi) has been caffeinating Bondi since 1997 and is my pick if coffee is the point. It grew from a hole-in-the-wall into a full café, with batch brew, espresso and cold drip plus a following for its matcha and specialty lattes. Best for: coffee-first locals and a quick, quality cup.
Sonoma - bakery coffee

[Sonoma](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/sonoma-bakery-cafe-bondi) is the well-known Sydney sourdough bakery with a Bondi outpost - a reliable stop for a proper coffee and a pastry or bakery-driven breakfast without the full brunch sit-down. If it's the pastry cabinet you're chasing, it sits alongside Bondi's other [bakeries and sweet spots](/bondi-eat-and-drink/bakeries-sweets-bondi-beach). Best for: a quick, high-quality grab-and-go.
Gertrude & Alice - Hall Street

Genuinely one of a kind: [Gertrude & Alice](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/gertrude-and-alice-cafe-bookstore) is a second-hand bookshop and café on Hall Street where you can settle in with Campos coffee, a Middle Eastern-leaning breakfast and a stack of books. It's the antidote to Bondi's see-and-be-seen rooms. Best for: a slow, quiet morning and something different.
Strong all-rounders just back from the sand
Blackwood - Glenayr Avenue

An Eastern Suburbs brunch staple a couple of streets back, [Blackwood](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/blackwood-bondi) is known for a seasonal menu that blends Mediterranean and Asian influences - ricotta pancakes, chilli scrambled eggs - with carefully made coffee. It's one of my go-tos when I want a considered sit-down away from the crowds; for more in that vein, see our [best breakfast and brunch guide](/bondi-eat-and-drink/breakfast-brunch-bondi-beach). Best for: a considered brunch away from the beachfront crush.
Porch and Parlour - North Bondi

A long-running North Bondi favourite (Ramsgate Avenue), [Porch & Parlour](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/porch-and-parlour) is built around local produce, with its well-known pea pancakes and a reliably buzzy weekend. It's also one of the better-known dog-friendly spots. Best for: a neighbourhood brunch with the dog in tow.
Newer and more unusual spots
Cafe Bondi - North Bondi (new)

One of the more recent openings, [Cafe Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/cafe-bondi) is on Campbell Parade at the North Bondi end and opens early for coffee, sunshine and an easy all-day menu. Best for: an early start at the quieter north end. (As a newer venue, double-check its days and hours before you rely on it.)
Up South - Bondi Road

Further up Bondi Road, [Up South](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/up-south-bondi) made its name on playful matcha creations and a rotating treats cabinet - the spot for a strawberry or pistachio matcha and a photo. Best for: matcha fans and a sweet mid-morning stop.
Lox, Stock & Barrel - bagels & deli

A Bondi take on a Jewish deli, [Lox, Stock & Barrel](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/lox-stock-and-barrel) is known for artisan bagels and generous, deli-influenced brunch plates. Best for: a bagel-led breakfast or an easy weekday lunch.
Makaveli & Pocket - café by day, bar by night

From the same team, [Makaveli](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/makaveli) (Glenayr Avenue) and [Pocket](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/pocket-bondi) (Campbell Parade) both work the café-to-cocktail-bar angle - pastries, loaded sourdough and coffee in the morning, share plates and drinks later. If it's the evening end that appeals, they also turn up in our [best Bondi bars](/bondi-eat-and-drink/best-bars-bondi-beach) roundup. Best for: a laid-back start that can roll into the afternoon.
A few more coffee windows worth knowing
Coffee is half the reason people love a Bondi morning, so beyond the rooms above here are a few more cups worth a short detour - handy when the beach-view spots are full.
Jacks North Bondi - Brighton Boulevard

An absolute North Bondi institution: the coffee window at the top of Brighton Boulevard that locals knew for years as Bru is now [Jacks](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bru-coffee-bondi), run by Jack Murat, who grows his own single-origin coffee up in Far North Queensland and pours it beachside here. It's the spot for the ritual every North Bondi swimmer knows - grab a flat white straight out of the water and dry off in the sun with a hot cup in hand, down on the grass or the sand. Little seating, mornings only, always humming. Best for: drying out with a coffee after a dip at the north end.
% Arabica - Bondi Beach

The Bondi outpost of the global specialty-coffee brand [% Arabica](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/arabica-bondi) trades on pared-back design and carefully sourced beans - a small destination if you take your coffee seriously. Best for: a considered espresso or matcha and a bit of coffee-world pedigree.
Will & Co - HQ tasting bar

Sydney roaster [Will & Co](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/will-and-co-hq-tasting-bar) runs an HQ tasting bar in Bondi - the spot to drink a local roaster's coffee close to the source. Best for: coffee drinkers who want to taste the roast.

A few more to keep in your back pocket: [Cortado](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/cortado-bondi-cafe) for an unfussy espresso away from the queues, the all-day [Bennett St Dairy](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bennett-st-dairy) a couple of streets back, and [Cali Press](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/cali-press) if you'd rather a cold-pressed juice or açai bowl than a coffee.
What's changed recently

Two things worth flagging for 2026. First, there's genuine new blood at the north end - Cafe Bondi being the clearest recent opening. Second, the former Hall Street all-day spot Bondi Hall has closed, so ignore older lists that still feature it. The refurbished Bondi Pavilion has also reopened with food and drink operators on the beachfront; those line-ups have shifted since the works, so check who's trading there now rather than trusting an older guide.
What to know before you go

items: Timing: arrive close to opening or after about 2pm to dodge the worst queues; weekend mornings are the busiest.
Booking: most Bondi cafés are walk-in, though a few take reservations for larger groups - check ahead if there are more than four of you.
Dogs: several are dog-friendly, with Porch and Parlour the best-known; outdoor tables are your friend.
Reusables: bring a keep-cup - some cafés knock a little off for it.
Make a morning of it: pair a café with the Saturday [Bondi Farmers Market](/whats-on/markets), or a swim first - see [where to swim at Bondi](/where-to-swim-at-bondi-beach).

blocks.text: Which Bondi café is right for you?

items: Best ocean view: Speedos Café (North Bondi).
Something different: Gertrude & Alice (bookshop café, Hall Street).
Best with a dog: Porch and Parlour (North Bondi).

items.q: What is the best café in Bondi?
items.a: It depends what you want. For a beachfront brunch with a view I'd point you to Speedos Café or Chapter One; for the best coffee, Harry's Bondi; and for an iconic Sydney breakfast, bills on Hall Street.

items.q: Which Bondi café has the best view?
items.a: Speedos Café at North Bondi and Chapter One on Campbell Parade both look straight out over the beach - the two I'd choose for a view-first breakfast.

items.q: Where is the best coffee in Bondi?
items.a: Harry's Bondi has been a coffee benchmark since 1997. Sonoma is a reliable bakery-coffee stop, Gertrude & Alice pours Campos in a bookshop setting, and for a serious cup it's worth seeking out % Arabica or roaster Will & Co.

items.q: Are there any new cafés in Bondi?
items.a: Cafe Bondi at the North Bondi end is one of the clearer recent openings. Note that the older Hall Street spot Bondi Hall has closed, so skip it on out-of-date lists.

items.q: Do I need to book a Bondi café?
items.a: Most are walk-in. Expect queues on weekend mornings, so arrive early or after about 2pm, and check ahead only if you're a larger group.

items.q: Are there dog-friendly cafés in Bondi?
items.a: Yes - Porch and Parlour in North Bondi is the best-known dog-friendly option, and many cafés welcome dogs at their outdoor tables.

blocks.title: Looking for more than ten?
blocks.text: This is my hand-picked shortlist, but it's a fraction of what's on the beach. Browse every café, restaurant, bar and bakery in [our full Bondi eat & drink directory](/bondi-eat-and-drink) - 160+ venues you can filter by cuisine, area, price and who you're with, from a quick coffee to a long lunch by the water.

However you play it, Bondi rewards a bit of café-hopping - a coffee at the north end, a swim, then brunch on Campbell Parade. For more on eating and drinking around the beach, see my [Bondi eat & drink guide](/bondi-eat-and-drink); for the rest of a day here, [things to do in Bondi](/things-to-do-in-bondi); and for markets and events, [what's on in Bondi](/whats-on).

blocks.text: If you're after the best vegetarian and vegan food in Bondi Beach, my short answer is this: start at [Funky Pies](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/funky-pies) for a fully vegan pie, graze your way through [Sabbaba](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/sabbaba-bondi-beach)'s falafel and salads, and finish with a [Gelato Messina](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/gelato-messina-bondi) sorbet on Hall Street. Bondi has quietly become one of Sydney's easiest suburbs to eat plant-based in, and after years of wandering these streets between swims, these are the spots I actually send friends to. If you'd rather see the whole field at a glance, we keep a running directory of Bondi's [best vegan and vegetarian spots](/bondi-eat-and-drink/vegan-vegetarian-bondi-beach).
Where I go for fully vegan food

Funky Pies, tucked away on Glenayr Avenue a short walk back from the sand, is the one I rate most highly for a proper hot meal. The whole menu is vegan - handmade, chunky pies and pastries, with the classics done properly rather than as an afterthought. It's a small shop with a cult following, so it's not somewhere you sit down for a long lunch; it's grab-a-pie-and-eat-it-on-the-grass energy, which is exactly what you want after a morning in the water. Check their site for current hours before you make a special trip.

For a lighter plant-based option, [Fishbowl](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/fishbowl) does a build-your-own poke-style bowl that's easy to keep fully vegan - tofu, brown rice, plenty of veg and a light dressing. It's a reliable, fast, post-beach lunch, and their online menu lists what's in each bowl if you have allergen questions.

Bondi's most beloved sweet spot is genuinely plant-based-friendly: at Gelato Messina on Hall Street the sorbets are dairy-free, and the chocolate sorbet in particular is so rich most people can't believe it's vegan. Check the vegan flavours list on the Messina site, since specials rotate weekly.
The best vegetarian-friendly eats

Sabbaba is my go-to for a cheap, generous veggie feed. It's a Middle Eastern street-food spot, and the vegetarians and vegans are genuinely looked after here - falafel pita stuffed with salad, hummus and tahini, plus dips, dolmades, chips and salads you can mix and match. It's fast, it's filling, and it's the kind of meal that suits a sandy, salty afternoon when you don't want to sit still for long. If a cheap, no-fuss feed is what you're chasing, it sits near the top of our roundup of Bondi's [best cheap eats](/bondi-eat-and-drink/cheap-eats-bondi-beach).

For brunch, the beachfront cafés along the promenade all carry solid vegetarian options these days - think smashed avo, grain bowls, veg-forward toasts and, at many, a vegan pancake or two. Menus and daily specials change constantly, so rather than promise you a specific dish, I'd say scan the board when you arrive and ask the staff what's vegan that day. In my experience they're used to the question and happy to help. If you want the full line-up before you set out, we've mapped Bondi's [best breakfast and brunch](/bondi-eat-and-drink/breakfast-brunch-bondi-beach) spots separately.
Bowls, açaí and sweeter plant-based treats

Bondi runs on smoothie bowls and açaí, and most of it is easy to keep plant-based. [OAKBERRY Açaí](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/oakberry-acai-bondi-beach) builds bowls on a naturally dairy-free açaí base - just swap the honey and choose your toppings - and [Cali Press](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/cali-press) is my pick for cold-pressed juices, smoothies and a veg-forward menu when I want something lighter than a pie. Both are the kind of quick, colourful refuel that suits a between-swims kind of day.

And if the queue at Messina is out the door, you're not stuck for something sweet. [Anita Gelato](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/anita-gelato-bondi) and [Rivareno Gelato](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/rivareno-gelato-bondi-beach) both scoop sorbets alongside their gelato, and [Yo-Chi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/yo-chi-bondi-beach) does self-serve frozen yoghurt where you assemble your own cup, sorbet options included. Ask which flavours are dairy-free on the day, since specials rotate everywhere. For the full sweet-tooth trail, see our guide to Bondi's [best bakeries and sweets](/bondi-eat-and-drink/bakeries-sweets-bondi-beach).
Fine dining with real vegetable dishes

[Icebergs Dining Room and Bar](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/icebergs-dining-room-and-bar), perched above the ocean pool, is best known for seafood, but it builds genuine, seasonal vegetable dishes into its menu too. It's a special-occasion place with a changing menu, so if you're vegetarian or vegan, phone ahead and mention it when you book so the kitchen can look after you properly. It's also one of a handful of [ocean-view dining rooms](/bondi-eat-and-drink/waterfront-dining-bondi-beach) in Bondi worth the splurge.

blocks.title: Menus move fast
blocks.text: Bondi's food scene turns over quickly - cafés change hands, hours shift with the seasons, and dishes rotate. I've pointed you at each venue's official channel rather than quoting prices or opening times that could be out of date by the time you visit. Always check the venue's own site or socials before heading out.

blocks.title: Find your own plant-based Bondi
blocks.text: These are my personal picks, but they're only a slice of what's here. Our [vegan and vegetarian directory](/bondi-eat-and-drink/vegan-vegetarian-bondi-beach) lists every plant-based-friendly spot in the suburb, and you can open the full [Bondi eat-and-drink guide](/bondi-eat-and-drink) to filter all 160+ venues by cuisine, area, price or who you're with.
How to plan a plant-based day in Bondi

items: Morning: coffee and a vegetarian brunch at a promenade café, or an açaí bowl from OAKBERRY, before it gets busy.
Midday: a swim, then a fully vegan pie from Funky Pies or a tofu bowl from Fishbowl.
Afternoon: a falafel and salad plate from Sabbaba to refuel.
Evening: a dairy-free sorbet from Gelato Messina, or book ahead for a seasonal vegetable menu at Icebergs.

items.q: Is Bondi Beach good for vegans?
items.a: Yes - it's one of the easier Sydney beach suburbs to eat vegan in. Funky Pies is entirely vegan, Fishbowl bowls can be built fully plant-based, Sabbaba has strong vegan options, and Gelato Messina's sorbets are dairy-free. Browsing our [vegan and vegetarian directory](/bondi-eat-and-drink/vegan-vegetarian-bondi-beach) is a good way to see everything that's nearby.

items.q: Where's the best fully vegan restaurant in Bondi?
items.a: For a hot, sit-down-style meal, Funky Pies on Glenayr Avenue is my top pick - the entire menu is vegan and the pies are handmade. Check their website for current opening hours before you go.

items.q: Can I get good vegetarian food at Bondi's fine-dining restaurants?
items.a: Yes. Icebergs Dining Room and Bar includes seasonal vegetable dishes on its menu. Because those menus change, phone ahead and flag that you're vegetarian or vegan when you book.

items.q: Is there vegan dessert in Bondi?
items.a: Gelato Messina on Hall Street is the classic choice - its sorbets are dairy-free, and the chocolate sorbet is a standout. Anita Gelato, Rivareno and Yo-Chi all offer plant-based options too. The flavours rotate, so check the current list in-store.

items.q: How do I know a café's options are actually vegan?
items.a: Ask. Bondi kitchens are very used to the question, daily specials change often, and staff can tell you what's plant-based that day - which is far more reliable than any menu photo online.

blocks.text: That's the loop I'd walk on a plant-based day here - a veggie brunch, a swim, something hearty and vegan for lunch, and a sorbet to finish. Bondi rewards eating the way it rewards everything else: slowly, with sand on your feet.
